decisions.text: The team decided against including a dedicated screen on the remote control due to the high cost of the advanced chip required.
The team agreed to use a spongy, stress-ball-like material for the main grip area of the remote.
The team will create two prototypes to test covering the squishy part versus other options and ask users for feedback.
The team decided to proceed with batteries as the power source for now.

notes:
## Component Design and Interface
- The team reviewed the last meeting's outcomes, including the targeted audience and the iPod-like button system concept which remains undecided.
- The team discussed using a wheel or a central button to control channels and menus on a TV screen, noting that a dedicated screen on the remote is too expensive.
- They considered a wheel that goes through at least a hundred channels, or a central button that brings up a menu on the TV for settings like brightness and timers.
## Material and Aesthetics
- Material options discussed are rubber, plastic, wood, and titanium; titanium is discouraged due to weight and flat-case limitations, and rubber is incompatible with plastic buttons.
- Marketing trends indicate a focus on a fancy look and feel, specifically a fruit and vegetable theme with a spongy feel.
- The remote should be smaller than previous concepts, possibly circular and handheld, using a spongy stress-ball-like material for comfort and a hard plastic section for the wheel.
- The team considered interchangeable covers featuring fruits or vegetables to match room decor, though silver fruit covers are not available.
- The product casing was described as silver and yellow.
## Product Shape and Prototyping
- The team debated whether the squishy part should be a detachable cover or a single unit that moulds to the hand like juggling balls.
- The idea of having interchangeable squishy parts representing different fruits and vegetables was discussed.
- The Industrial Designer noted that changing the shape every time a new part is swapped might be inconvenient.
- The Industrial Designer explained that the squishy part needs to be a single unit that can snap off to allow battery access.
## Power Source and Manufacturing
- The team considered batteries, solar power, a dynamo (bicycle mechanism), and a kinetic wind-up option.
- The Marketing Expert expressed a preference for the dynamo because it generates energy on its own without needing batteries.
- The Industrial Designer noted that solar power seems unsuitable for a rubber case in a living room setting.
- The Industrial Designer clarified that 'chip on print' refers to mass-producing chips stamped onto the device, similar to remote controls, making them cheap.
- The Industrial Designer identified the chip as likely being the most expensive part of the device.
tldr: The team reviewed component designs and material options, deciding against a dedicated screen on the remote due to cost. They settled on a spongy, stress-ball-like grip with interchangeable fruit or vegetable covers and agreed to proceed with batteries as the power source while testing prototypes.
